verdict.rationale: The desktop app can install and run MCP connectors on your machine or local network, and it can connect local agents, including external coding CLIs. It also has a built-in terminal with multiple sessions. Together these point to some local execution surface, but none of the evidence says LobeHub's own assistant natively runs shell commands or edits files. Execution appears to depend on third-party MCP tools or connected external agents. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation that the agent executes commands and edits files, a documented link between the agent and the desktop terminal, permission/approval controls, and hands-on corroboration.
